Total cost per student ($15,335) sits in the middle of the six neighbors and $424 under the peer average. It is above the two similar-size county districts (Alcorn $13,258, Itawamba $12,308) and below the three smaller municipal districts (Booneville, Corinth, Baldwyn), which carry heavier debt and capital costs per student.
Instruction per student ($8,949) is within $12 of the peer average.
General administration per student ($399) is the second lowest of the seven and 41% below the peer average. School-level administration ($837) is the second highest, 17% above the peer average.
Instruction share (58.4%) is below Alcorn, Prentiss and Itawamba (62–66%) and above the three municipal districts.
Local taxpayers carry a larger share in Tishomingo (32.4% of revenue) than in Alcorn, Prentiss or Itawamba (20–29%); property tax per student ($3,647) is the second highest after Baldwyn.
Reserves: 5.2 months of General Fund spending on hand, versus 2–3 months at Alcorn, Itawamba and Booneville. Corinth is the outlier at 12.4 months.
Debt is the lowest of the seven at $889 per student after FY2025 payoffs; net pension liability per student is in line with peers (it is set by the state system, not the district).

Audit findings: four of the six neighbors had zero state-law findings in their latest audit. TCSD had four, all repeats from prior years; Booneville had three repeats; Itawamba (FY2023) had five plus a material weakness.
Superintendent pay ($131,500) is below the peer average ($155,152) and the lowest per student except Itawamba.
